item.title: Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called on Nigerian youths to shun campaign of division, segregation, discrimination and marginalisation. Obasanjo made the call on Saturday after receiving an honorary doctorate degree conferred on him by the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. He was conferred with the honour alongside former Executive Secretary, National Universities Commission (NUC), Prof. Abubakar Adamu-Rasheed and Mrs. Vadana Luthra. The former president, who addressed the gathering through a recorded video, said the youths, irrespective of their tribe, religion and age, must be the architects of their own future and fortune, noting they have to struggle for what they want, as salvation will not come from heaven. He said himself, and the late Head of State Murtala Muhammad spearheaded the change in the country. Obasanjo said the youths have to be positively disruptive to bring about the desired change. “Most of the leaders of the immediate, pre and post-independent era were young and active. “They went for change, and they made it happen. Nigeria, as a whole, benefited from their activism. “Let me name two – Aminu Kano and Enahoro. The military era was not much different.” Earlier, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ajith Kumar, announced approval of new programmes by the National Universities Commission (NUC), adding that the university was the first in North-West Nigeria to receive approval for the B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence programme. He said the development further demonstrates its commitment to advancing technology-driven education in the region. Kumar said the institution has awarded a 50% scholarship to all toppers to pursue their postgraduate programmes at the university. A total of 237 students graduated with various degrees at the institution’s 5th convocation ceremony. (NAN) The post Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. item.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway. The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. (NAN) The post FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain
item.description: Super Eagles forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying return-leg fixture against Tanzania following a knee ligament sprain. Promise Efoghe, Super Eagles Media Officer, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday. “Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match. “This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Efoghe said. The injury was sustained during Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday. Lookman’s absence will be a setback for the Super Eagles as they prepare for the return fixture against the Taifa Stars. The Athletico Madrid forward has been an important attacking option for Nigeria, providing creativity, pace and goal-scoring threat in the final third. NAN reports that Friday’s victory strengthened Nigeria’s position in the qualifying campaign, taking their points tally to six. The Super Eagles will now travel to Zanzibar for Tuesday’s Matchday Four encounter, hoping to consolidate their position in the group. Nigeria will be seeking another positive result against Tanzania as the race for qualification for the 2027 AFCON finals gathers momentum. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already guaranteed places at the tournament as co-hosts, leaving the remaining qualification spots to be contested by other countries. The 2027 AFCON finals will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. (NAN) The post Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra. “We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said. Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria. item.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
item.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. He noted that Nigeria’s enormous human and natural resources should have translated into comparable levels of development, questioning the obstacles that had continued to constrain the country’s potential. item.title: Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened
item.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials. The mission was responding to South African Presidency spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who accused Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa’s intervention following a disagreement over the omission of his address during Friday’s credentials presentation ceremony in Tshwane. In a strongly worded statement posted on X, the Nigerian High Commission accused Magwenya of making provocative and undiplomatic remarks, warning that his comments could undermine diplomatic relations between both countries. The commission said Magwenya had accused Fani-Kayode of lying and disgracing Nigeria barely hours after the envoy presented his letters of credence to the South African President. “You are the disgrace and no-one else. Outside of that your insolence and ignorance knows no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and wilfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said. The controversy followed the apparent disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream around the time Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa. The broadcast subsequently resumed when the South African President was addressing the ambassadors. Fani-Kayode, who was the last diplomat to present his credentials, had expressed displeasure over the omission of his address from the ceremony. He said he subsequently spoke with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him that everything was fine. However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement. The commission also recalled an earlier controversy in which Magwenya reportedly described concerns expressed by President Bola Tinubu and Ghanaian President John Mahama over xenophobia and Afrophobia in South Africa as fake news. It said Nigeria had ignored the earlier remarks but questioned why Magwenya would publicly describe its newly accredited envoy as a liar. “Did you really expect him to simply stomach your ill manners and keep quiet? If so you have misunderstood the character and nature of the Nigerian. We cannot be easily cowed,” the statement added. The mission further disclosed that several people, including newly accredited ambassadors from other countries, witnessed the proceedings and expressed displeasure over what transpired. It also claimed to possess a full video recording of the proceedings after the official photographs were taken, adding that it could release the footage if authorised to do so. item.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
item.description: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”. He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”. It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”. But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. item.title: ‘Obi ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‌⁠‌‌​is incorruptible,’ says Kwankwaso
item.description: The vice presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has described the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as incorruptible. Kwankwaso made the declaration on Saturday at the 5th convocation ceremony of the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. Kwankwaso said the attribute is key and needed in governance of the nation. “One thing I noted in the last few months that we have been working together is that Peter Obi is incorruptible. He’s not somebody that you can go and start thinking of corruption around him, and that is very key in governance in this country,” he said. Kwankwaso pledged that an NDC-led administration would prioritise free education to ensure that no child was denied access to schooling due to financial constraints. “We have so much in common, especially in the issue of education. We believe that together it will be extremely difficult to see how any child will go around in this part of the country or elsewhere begging for what to eat. “In other words, we are working towards free education to ensure that our children are not denied going to school because the parents cannot afford to pay school fees or other expenses. In his remarks, Obi pledged to revive moribund industries in Kano to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities. He described Kano as central to Nigeria’s economic development, saying efforts to rebuild the country’s economy must begin with the state. “If we want to fix the North and Nigeria, we must start from Kano. This town represents the soul of Nigeria,” he said. Obi urged the graduates to embrace entrepreneurship, noting that small businesses play a critical role in employment generation and economic growth. item.title: Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Portugal have announced a redesign of the No. 7 on their national team shirts in tribute to former captain Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced the change on Saturday, saying the new design would preserve the legacy of the number associated with the 41-year-old forward. In a statement shared by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, the federation said the decision was another way to immortalise the significance of the number and honour Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese football. “This is another way to eternalise the meaning of such a special number and honour the legacy it represents for us. “Because there are stories, memories, all the achievements and emotions, which will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the sweater, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalisation of the story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the statement read. Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on November 5, bringing an end to his 23-year international career. In a message to Portuguese supporters, the forward said it was time to hand back the national team shirt and captain’s armband after enjoying the privilege of representing his country for more than two decades. “For 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world,” he said. Ronaldo finished his international career as Portugal’s record appearance-maker, with 234 caps, and all-time leading scorer, with 146 goals. He also captained the country to its first European Championship title in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025. item.title: Yilwatda charges North-Central APC leaders to unite for Tinubu
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has charged governors, governorship candidates and party leaders across the North-Central region to unite stakeholders and intensify mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Yilwatda gave the charge at the APC presidential campaign rally held at Azaria Road Stadium, Jos, Plateau State, where Tinubu’s campaign train received a large turnout of party leaders, supporters and residents. The APC national chairman expressed satisfaction with the turnout and what he described as a renewed spirit of unity among party leaders and supporters in Plateau State. He urged residents to translate the enthusiasm demonstrated at the rally into votes, insisting that the state must deliver a record-breaking victory for Tinubu. Yilwatda declared that political leaders in Plateau State were fully united behind the President, assuring him that the support demonstrated at the rally would be reflected at the ballot box. He also described Tinubu as a promise keeper who had fulfilled his commitments to Plateau State, saying the administration’s performance provided a basis for continued public support. A major highlight of the rally was the presentation of APC flags to the party’s governorship candidates across the North-Central states, in what the party described as a demonstration of its commitment to strengthening its political structures and securing victory at all levels. Speaking further, Yilwatda urged APC governors, governorship candidates and party leaders in the region to set aside personal interests and political differences, unite all stakeholders and work towards a common electoral objective. In Plateau State, he urged party leaders to consolidate the unity already achieved and mobilise support for Tinubu and all APC candidates. In Benue State, he called on the governor and party leaders to harmonise competing interests, bring political stakeholders together and mobilise voters for the party. For Niger State, the APC chairman expressed confidence in the state leadership’s ability to use the party’s flag as a rallying point to unite members and secure victory for Tinubu and other candidates. Similarly, while presenting the party’s flag to its governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Wadada, Yilwatda urged him and other party leaders to provide purposeful leadership, unite stakeholders and mobilise support for the President. He also called for concerted efforts towards greater prosperity, peace and development in the state. The APC chairman stressed that the North-Central region must approach the 2027 elections with a common purpose, urging party structures, elected officials, candidates and grassroots mobilisers to intensify engagement with voters. item.title: Atiku tackles FG as bakers lose 40% membership
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies for the loss of nearly 40 per cent of the membership of the Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria in two years, warning that soaring energy costs and high interest rates are driving local businesses out of operation. The development, he said, underscores the growing strain on businesses, with bakeries shutting down, workers losing their jobs and households paying more for bread, one of Nigeria’s everyday staples. Atiku, who was in Bauchi on Saturday to promote his affordable life campaign and sympathise with Nigerians grappling with the effects of government policies, spoke in a statement signed by his Director of Strategic Communication, ADC Presidential Campaign Council, and Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Phrank Shaibu. “From farmers to manufacturers and now bakers, the verdict on Tinubu’s economic reforms cannot be clearer: they have been a monumental failure,” he said. The former vice president identified rising energy costs and expensive credit as major constraints on bakery operations, noting that energy alone accounts for about half of production costs. He cited the case of a bakery operator whose monthly diesel bill reportedly increased from N9 million to N19 million, while small-scale bakeries require between N40 million and N50 million to switch to alternative energy sources. He added that businesses seeking loans face interest rates of up to 34 per cent, further limiting their ability to sustain production and invest in more efficient operations. Atiku said the pressure extends beyond the baking industry, citing rising cooking gas prices, which he said had reached N1,800 per kilogramme in Abuja and N1,650 in parts of Lagos and Ogun states. He also cited a 31.8 per cent increase in depot prices within one month, from N1,100 to N1,450 per kilogramme. Turning to the Federal Government’s borrowing, Atiku questioned the accumulation of domestic and foreign loans amid the reported closure of local businesses, alleging that Nigerians were yet to see tangible benefits from the debt. “The irony is that while the economy is falling under Bola Tinubu’s watch, his government has accumulated local and foreign loans in astronomical figures. If local businesses are dying while the government continues to borrow, Nigerians are entitled to ask where these loans are going. One is forced to conclude that they are feeding the corruption in Tinubu’s government,” he said. He called for a shift in economic priorities towards strengthening domestic production across sectors, rather than concentrating exclusively on crude oil refining. “The major policy plank of my administration will be to improve local production in every sphere of the economy, not just crude oil refining. “To farmers, manufacturers, bakers and everyone involved in local production: the Atiku Economic Recovery Plan understands your pains, and your con

item.title: Spain will host 2030 World Cup final, federation president insists
item.description: The 2030 World Cup final will be in Spain, Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) head Rafael Louzan reiterated on Saturday, adding that he is not considering “withdrawing” should he be wrong. Spain is organising the next World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. The decision on the venue for the final will be made in 2028, Louzan said. Spain favours Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium for the final. Portugal does not have a suitable stadium but Morocco has suggested the 115,000-capacity Hassan II Stadium being built in Benslimane near Casablanca. “There is no other plan than for the final to be held in Spain,” said Louzan at a conference at the RFEF’s Ciudad del Futbol on the outskirts of Madrid. “I am not currently considering the possibility of withdrawing from Spain, as the prospect of Spain not hosting the final is not on the table,” he said. Louzan was responding to Alberto Nunez Feijoo, the leader of the right-wing People’s Party. In a television interview on November 5, Feijoo said that were he to become prime minister in the general election on November 29, he would advocate withdrawing Spain’s bid to host the World Cup should Morocco be awarded the final. Luzon said the question was entirely hypothetical. “That notion simply doesn’t exist,” he said, adding that under FIFA’s tradition of rotating the World Cup the staging of the final “belongs to the European continent”. A delegation of FIFA technical experts spent last week visiting Spanish stadiums that are hoping to host matches during the tournament, Louzan said. item.title: 2027: I’ll restore fuel subsidy, tackle insecurity if elected — Atiku vows
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi & Ayobami Okerinde Former Vice-President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Atiku Abubakar has promised to restore fuel subsidy and tackle insecurity if elected president. Atiku made the pledge on Saturday during the ADC presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State, where he urged residents to vote for candidates of the party across all elective positions. “I have already promised all Nigerians that I will restore petroleum subsidy. Not only that, I will also restore subsidy in electricity,” he said. Atiku also pledged to address insecurity in the Northeast and other parts of the country, while promising to expand petroleum exploration in the Kolmani area to generate additional revenue. He called on Nigerians to support the ADC, urging voters in Bauchi to elect the party’s candidates from the presidency to the councillorship positions. The former vice-president thanked the people of the state for their previous support, saying Bauchi had consistently given him substantial votes in past elections. He urged residents to turn out in large numbers during the 2027 polls and ensure their votes were protected and counted. “I want you to make sure you come out in your thousands. You vote for ADC. You defend the vote. You ensure that the votes are counted, and results are transmitted before you leave the polling booth,” Atiku said. President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy on May 29, 2023, during his inauguration, declaring that “the fuel subsidy is gone”. He said the funds would instead be redirected to infrastructure, education, healthcare and job creation. Atiku has repeatedly promised to restore petrol subsidy if elected in 2027. In August , he reiterated the pledge, questioning how the savings from its removal had been spent. The former vice president was accompanied by his running mate and former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, and other party leaders, said his administration would prioritise policies aimed at alleviating the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. Also associated with the Bauchi campaign delegation was the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Senator Halliru Dauda Jika, alongside other ADC chieftains and political stakeholders. item.title: Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has asked families affected by the deadly attacks in Anguwan Rukuba , in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State that left many killed and several injured in March 2026, to forgive him for not visiting the communities. ﻿ Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-Central presidential campaign rally in Jos on Saturday. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport. Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland. But I saw the devastation; I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people. “But since then, that has changed; we are forging together. He, however, assured residents that their communities would be rebuilt for those displaced to return home. Tinubu said too many lives had been lost to attacks in Plateau since 2001. He condoled with families who have lost loved ones to such attacks. Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), called for unity, saying speaking different languages should not lead to divisions. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau. “What we should be getting is prosperity, not havoc, not crisis. Our government is not elected to inflict wounds on one another or to bury people. We have to lift people up from penury to prosperity. “One thousand forest guards are undergoing training right now. You will feel them; you will see them. You will feel secure in your villages and communities,” he added. The President also said the surveillance cameras had been procured as promised. Tinubu assured the residents that his government his working to ease their suffering. A deadly attack in Anguwan Rukuba, in Jos North Local Government Area of the state in March, 2026, left at least 20 people killed and many others injured. On April 2, Tinubu met with the affected families at the Jos Airport, where he condoled with them and assured them that such an incident would not recur. ﻿ The President was criticised for not visiting the affected communities, but his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga , said that said the visit was affected by a scheduled meeting with the President of Chad. The post Forgive Me If You Didn’t See Me In The Hinterlands,’ Tinubu Tells Plateau Attack Victims appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Kwankwaso’s daughter seeks divorce from Kano gov, offers to refund dowry
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The second wife of Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, has filed for divorce at an Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, offering to refund the dowry paid by the governor. Zainab, a daughter of former Kano State Governor Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, is seeking to dissolve the marriage through Khul’i, an Islamic procedure that allows a woman to seek divorce by returning her dowry or offering compensation. According to court documents, the court has summoned Governor Yusuf to appear on November 17, 2026, to respond to the suit. In her claim, Zainab cited a breakdown of the marriage, alleging a persistent lack of love, care, affection and emotional connection. She also told the court that efforts to reconcile them had failed and expressed willingness to refund the dowry paid on their wedding day. Zainab married Yusuf on July 29, 2006, and their marriage produced six children. Her divorce suit comes weeks after she reportedly left the Kano Government House for her father’s residence before travelling to Abuja. item.title: Microsoft announces service ‘restored,’ global outage over
item.description: Tech giant Microsoft said Saturday it has “restored service” to customers, effectively drawing a close to a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and business around the world. “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the US-based company said in an X post. Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents.” The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company’s products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector. Microsoft had attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure. It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant. item.title: 2027: We won’t allow religion to divide us, Makinde declares
item.description: …seeks Muslim community’s support for Adekanmbi By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), ‘Seyi Makinde, has declared that his administration will not allow religious differences to divide the people of the state, insisting that they share a common ancestry and must remain united irrespective of their faith. Makinde, who made the declaration on Saturday, also appealed to Muslim leaders across the state to use their influence to promote unity, peace and political stability ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor spoke at the opening of a three-day conference for Imams, Alfas/Ulama, political office holders and traditional rulers, tagged Rabitah 2026, organised by the League of Imams and Alfas in Yoruba Land (Rabitah tul Aimma wal Hulammai fii Biladi Yoruba) at the Jogor Event Centre, Ibadan. The conference, with the theme, “The Responsibilities of Politicians and Electorate During and After Electoral Process,“ brought together prominent Islamic clerics, scholars, traditional rulers and political stakeholders from across the South-West. Makinde noted that discussions surrounding the choice of the next governor of the state had intensified ahead of the elections, urging political and religious stakeholders not to allow such developments to create divisions along religious lines. “We won’t allow religion to divide us. Let us pray for our state and country because this is the period leading to the next election, when a new set of leaders will emerge.“ “There is a lot of discussion going on right now about the choice of who will become the next governor.“ “What matters most is that we must stay united. The progress of Oyo State is what is important to us, and I believe God will answer our prayers. For us in Oyo State, religion is not an issue.“ “We have all religions in our various families, and we have always coexisted peacefully,” he said. Makinde further illustrated the historical and familial connections between Muslims and Christians in Oyo State, disclosing that his own family background reflected the religious diversity he was advocating. He said: “I, standing before you, am Oluseyi Makinde. “Makinde was my grandfather on my father’s side. My father’s name is Olatunbosun, and my grandfather, Makinde, lived and died as a Muslim. item.title: ‘It’s unfortunate’ – Melaye reacts to Galadima’s claim on Justice Lifu’s illness
item.description: Dino Melaye has described as unfortunate elder statesman Buba Galadima’s comments linking him to discussions surrounding the health of Federal High Court judge, Justice Peter Lifu. Melaye said he never made any comment about Lifu’s health, noting “I was extremely shocked to hear that Alhaji Buba Galadima mentioned that I made comments on Justice Lifu’s health. “It is most unfortunate because I never made any comment on Justice Lifu’s health. “Old age must be catching up with Buba Galadima. Now I know you can’t cure old age, you can only manage it,” he wrote on his X (Twitter) page. Galadima had criticised members of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, over their reported reaction to Lifu’s health. In an interview on African Independent Television, AIT, on Wednesday, Galadima mentioned Melaye while referring to information that the ADC had obtained a certified true copy of the judgment delivered against the party. Galadima, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, said: “You know there was a judgment against ADC, isn’t it? Yes. And I’ve just heard you read something that Dino Melaye said. “They’ve got a true certified copy of the judgment, and I know some ADC people are jumping up and down that the judge (Peter Lifu) who gave a ruling against them has fallen ill and is supposed to be taken to hospital in Europe. “I just found out that maybe there aren’t intelligent people in the ADC. They didn’t know that if that is true, it is deliberate to deny them appeal. Because if the judge goes to London or Europe or anywhere outside the country, the records of proceedings from his judgment cannot be signed by any judge. “So no appeal could be had until he’s back. They didn’t know that they are playing on their intelligence, and that’s why Nigerian politicians are lazy.
